To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) elementary school students' intrinsic motivation develops over the school year; (2) students' perceptions of teacher support and need satisfaction are related to their motivation; (3) students' motivation is related to their engagement; and (4) students' self-reported engagement is related to their teachers' assessments.

(1) students' motivation, need satisfaction, engagement, and perceptions of teacher support were positively associated; (2) students' self reported motivation and engagement were positively correlated with external raters' assessments; (3) students' motivation and need satisfaction were positively associated with teacher reports of students' motivation; and (4) students' motivation at the beginning of the school year was a strong predictor of their motivation at the end of the school year.
the quality of the learning environment and the students' engagement are important for the development of self-determined motivation in elementary school students' foreign language classes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of motivation over time, with the role of teachers' instructional practices in this development, and with the relationship between teachers' and students' assessments of the quality of motivation.
how the learning environment in elementary foreign language classrooms can support students' motivation and engagement.
how motivation develops over the long term and how the quality of students’ motivation is assessed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study has provided a longitudinal model of how elementary school children's self-determined motivation develops in a foreign language class, and that the findings can provide a foundation for further studies on motivation in foreign language education.
the results of this study support the idea that a supportive environment and positive teacher student relationships are essential to motivating elementary school language learners.

the Japanese public schools' foreign language instruction provided an environment that supported intrinsic motivation and engagement, and that students' self determination and motivation were dynamic, developing over time in response to their learning environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the students' motivation was positively related to the quality of their learning and engagement.
the students in this study were motivated to learn English and were able to maintain that motivation throughout the school year.
students' motivation, engagement, and perceptions of the learning context are interrelated and mutually supportive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of instruction in foreign language classrooms is a critical determinant of students' motivation to learn the target language.
students' motivation and engagement are dynamic processes.
the quality of the learning experience is more important to students' motivation and engagement than the quantity of the experience.
